subject: On-prem licensing: bundle, platform fee amortization & support tiers
messages:
From: Elliot Harper <elliot.harper@novasystems.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novasystems.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem licensing questions and packaging options

Monica —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. We're close to internal approval but procurement asked for more clarity on three items before we move to legal:

1) Platform fee amortization — can the platform fee be spread over the first 12 months of a 36‑month on‑prem contract?
2) Support tiers — we need a clear delineation between "Standard" and "Enterprise" SLA (response times, included oncall hours, escalation).
3) Add‑ons and seats vs nodes — our infra team prefers node counts, but our finance team wants a predictable amortized fee.

Can you send a short commercial note with examples (numbers) and an updated SOW draft showing the amortization?

Appreciate it —
Elliot
Procurement Lead, Nova Systems
attachments: none
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Harper <elliot.harper@novasystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem licensing questions and packaging options

Elliot —

Thanks — happy to clarify. High level answers below; I'm attaching a short commercial summary and a draft SOW with an amortization example. See attachments: redwood_onprem_pricing_v3.pdf and nova_requested_sow_draft.docx.

1) Platform fee amortization: yes — we can propose a 12/36 amortization schedule where 1/3 of the platform fee is recognized each year. For commercial flexibility we can also do an even 36‑month spread; the discounting/credits change slightly depending on recognition.

Example (illustrative):
- Platform fee list: $180,000 for 36 months (one time at signature)
- 12/36 amortization: Year1 expense for Nova = $60,000 (recognize internally as credit)
- This enables Nova to show lower first‑year burden; Redwood treats platform fee as prepay for SOW purposes.

2) Support tiers:
- Standard: business hours (M‑F 9–5 local) email + ticket; 24h response for Sev1; 72h for Sev2. Includes 10 oncall hours per month (billed overage at $250/hr).
- Enterprise: 24/7 paged oncall, 4h response Sev1, 8h Sev2; includes 40 oncall hours per month and quarterly operational reviews. Enterprise also includes an annual incident table and routing SLA.

3) Seats vs nodes:
- We can price by nodes (preferred for on‑prem). Example: Starter (4 nodes), Production (10 nodes), scale bands thereafter. We can provide a blended seat equivalence if finance needs a headcount metric.

Next steps: I propose a short call (30m) with procurement + finance + infra to run through the numbers and land on a preferred amortization and support tier. Are you available Friday morning PST?

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: On-prem licensing questions and packaging options

Forwarding Elliot's ask — good summary from you. A few internal points before we lock numbers:

- We should preserve NRR economics: if we allow 12/36 amortization, propose a modest concession in platform fee (5–8%) or commit to a 3‑year minimum to protect unit economics.
- For support, let's make Enterprise include two named oncall rotations (to limit blowouts) and tie any >50% overage to a capped quarterly true‑up.
- For node pricing: add a migration retainer line item (one‑time) so we don't underprice implementation effort.

I've drafted two optional price decks (attached as a redline in the pricing PDF) — one aggressive concession, one conservative. We'll pick the conservative as our default but present both to Nova.

Marissa
VP, Commercial
From: Elliot Harper <elliot.harper@novasystems.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novasystems.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 10:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem licensing questions and packaging options

Monica / team —

Thanks for the quick answers and the SOW draft. A few follow ups from procurement after internal review:

- Nova is comfortable with the 12/36 amortization if Redwood can offer a 7% credit on the platform fee and cap the implementation retainer at $45k.
- Procurement would like the Enterprise support SLA to explicitly state "two named on‑call engineers included; overtime billed at $200/hr up to a quarterly cap of 80 hours."
- Our infra director asked for node licensing examples for 6 and 12 node clusters with expected throughput and recommended padding. Can you provide those (ballpark numbers fine) so we can map to capacity planning?

If you can turn these items around by EOD Thursday we can route to legal next week.

—Elliot
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Harper <elliot.harper@novasystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem licensing questions and packaging options

Elliot —

Appreciate the specifics. Confirming Redwood's counter below so you can take to legal: 

1) Platform fee: Redwood accepts a 7% credit on the platform fee (applies at signature). List price was $180,000; net after 7% = $167,400. Amortization 12/36 remains in the commercial summary and will be reflected in the SOW payment schedule.

2) Implementation retainer: capped at $45,000 one‑time (we'll include an itemized migration plan).

3) Support SLA: update to include two named oncall engineers, overtime billed at $200/hr, quarterly cap 80 hours. We'll add language around true‑ups and a quarterly reconciliation process.

4) Node examples: attached a short appendix with throughput guidance for 6‑node and 12‑node bundles (ballpark TPS and concurrent session estimates) — included in redwood_onprem_pricing_v3.pdf appendix.

Next steps: I'll upload the revised SOW to DocuSign and share the HubSpot deal link once updated. If that plan looks good, I'll follow up with a single doc for Legal to redline.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_onprem_pricing_v3.pdf (contains price deck + node appendix)
